purpose: Contract each fixed-length component of the complementary 2-factor of a Hamiltonian 4-regular graph into one constant-domain state. Separate each local proper colouring into an S3-orbit type and a local colour gauge, so every Hamiltonian edge becomes a very small relative-gauge avoidance constraint. This isolates the first genuine local state jump: triangles have one orbit, while C4 already has three.

cycle_orbit_count.free_action: S3 acts freely on proper 3-colourings of C_k: a proper colouring uses at least two colours, and a colour permutation fixing all used colours is the identity.

boundary.k3: r_3=1. A triangle has a single proper-colouring orbit under colour renaming.
boundary.k4: r_4=3. A square is the first cycle with a nontrivial local orbit-type choice.
boundary.interpretation: The cycle-plus-triangles regime has no local type bit beyond an S3 gauge. Starting at length four, an additional finite local type variable appears.

signatures.T0: both opposite pairs equal: c0=c2 and c1=c3

c4_canonical_types.uniqueness: Every proper C4 colouring is uniquely g composed with one representative T_tau, with tau in {0,1,2} and g in S3. Hence the 18 proper colourings equal 3 orbit types times 6 gauges.

global_quotient.input: A 4-regular graph G supplied as the edge-disjoint union of a Hamiltonian cycle H and a complementary 2-factor F whose components all have one fixed length k.
global_quotient.component_state: For every F-component X choose an orbit type tau_X in {1,...,r_k} and a gauge g_X in S3, relative to a fixed canonical representative rho_tau of that orbit.
global_quotient.automatic_F_legality: The representative rho_tau is a proper colouring of the F-cycle, and composition by g_X preserves inequality, so every F-edge is satisfied automatically.
global_quotient.hamiltonian_edge: If a Hamiltonian edge joins port p of component X to port q of component Y, require g_X(rho_tauX[p]) != g_Y(rho_tauY[q]).
global_quotient.relative_gauge_form: For X!=Y put h=g_Y^{-1} g_X. With a=rho_tauX[p] and b=rho_tauY[q], the edge forbids h(a)=b. Exactly two of the six elements of S3 map a to b, so each edge forbids one size-two coset and allows four relative gauges.
global_quotient.same_component_edge: If a Hamiltonian edge has both endpoints in one F-component, the gauge cancels and the constraint is the pure type test rho_tau[p]!=rho_tau[q].
global_quotient.global_symmetry: Simultaneous left composition g_X -> pi g_X for all components preserves every constraint. For a nonempty connected instance one root gauge may therefore be fixed to the identity without loss.
global_quotient.equivalence: G is 3-colourable iff this finite-domain orbit-plus-gauge CSP is satisfiable. A CSP solution reconstructs the vertex colouring componentwise in linear time, and every graph colouring maps back uniquely after choosing canonical orbit representatives.

quotient_multigraph.definition: Contract every F-component to one node and retain the Hamiltonian edges as a labelled multigraph Q, with labels recording the endpoint ports.
quotient_multigraph.degree: A length-k component contains k vertices and therefore 2k Hamiltonian half-edges; Q is 2k-regular counting loop incidences.
quotient_multigraph.euler_structure: The original Hamiltonian cycle becomes a distinguished Euler tour of Q using every quotient edge exactly once. Thus the constraint graph is not arbitrary: it is a bounded-degree Eulerian multigraph with a supplied Euler tour and port labels.

source_boundary.positive_triangle_fact: Fleischner-Stiebitz prove that a Hamiltonian cycle plus vertex-disjoint triangles is always 3-colourable (indeed 3-choosable). In the quotient language this is exactly the one-orbit r_3=1 regime.
source_boundary.harder_cycle_fact: Fleischner-Sabidussi prove NP-completeness for 4-regular Hamiltonian graphs whose complementary components are non-selfcrossing cycles of constant length at least four. Therefore constant local component size and non-selfcrossing structure do not by themselves imply tractability.
source_boundary.firewall: The artifact uses the source theorem only at the class level stated above; it does not assume a stronger unverified claim that every individually fixed k>=4 is NP-complete. The exact quotient construction itself is valid for every fixed k.

positive: Replaces O(k) vertex colours inside each complementary cycle by one constant-size orbit type plus one S3 gauge.
Identifies the first local structural jump exactly: r_3=1 versus r_4=3.
Turns all Hamiltonian constraints into size-two forbidden relative-gauge cosets on a bounded-degree Eulerian quotient multigraph.
Provides immediate linear-time witness reconstruction from any quotient solution.
anti_loop: Do not enumerate (6*r_k)^(number of F-components) states.

Do not claim that fixed component size, a supplied Euler tour, or non-selfcrossing of individual components yields a polynomial DP; the cited hard source already has constant-size complementary cycles.

Do not promote the always-colourable triangle case to a constructive polynomial terminal without a proved colouring algorithm; published proofs are non-algorithmic and the search complexity has been explicitly noted as open.

next_target.name: E8_S3_RELATIVE_GAUGE_COSET_CONTRACTION_V5_4
next_target.directive: Attack the quotient CSP rather than the original graph. Exploit simultaneously: constant orbit-type set, S3 gauges, each intercomponent Hamiltonian edge forbids exactly a two-element relative-gauge coset, Q is bounded-degree Eulerian with a supplied Euler tour, and port labels originate from non-selfcrossing constant-size F-cycles. Seek a polynomial group-gain/minimax contraction or prove a scoped barrier. Do not enumerate component states or generic treewidth boundary assignments.

sources: H. Fleischner and M. Stiebitz, A solution to a colouring problem of P. Erdos, Discrete Mathematics 101 (1992), 39-48.
H. Fleischner and G. Sabidussi, 3-colorability of 4-regular hamiltonian graphs, Journal of Graph Theory 42(2) (2003), 125-140.
K. Berczi and Y. Kobayashi, An algorithm for identifying cycle-plus-triangles graphs, Discrete Applied Mathematics 226 (2017), 10-16.
